title: ML 系统设计面试 第 2 章 · 视觉搜索系统 — 专业书籍精读 Book 83
title_en: ML System Design Interview Ch 2 · Visual Search System — Books Deep-Read Book 83

questions.question: 设计十亿级图库的以图搜图时，有人提议训练一个二分类模型：输入两张图，输出「像 / 不像」。这个方案的致命问题是什么？
options: 二分类只能处理同一尺寸的图片，用户上传的图片尺寸不一，无法直接输入
二分类模型的准确率天然低于对比学习，必须换成更大的网络才能达到可用精度
每次查询都要对全库每张图做一次推理，十亿次推理在工程上不可行
二分类需要大量负样本，而图库中不相似的图片太少，训练数据不够
questions.explanation: 书里说这个方案的致命伤不在准确率，而在算力形状：查询时要和全库逐一配对推理。把问题改成表示学习后，全库离线各编码一次，查询只需 1 次推理加一次向量检索。把问题归结为准确率不够、换大模型，正好漏掉了这道题真正考的问题转化。
questions.question_en: For image search over a billion-image library, someone proposes a binary classifier that takes two images and outputs "similar / not similar." What's the fatal flaw?
options_en: Binary classifiers only accept fixed-size inputs, and user uploads vary in size, so they can't be fed in directly
Binary classifiers are inherently less accurate than contrastive learning, so only a much bigger network would reach usable accuracy
Every query would need an inference against every library image—a billion inferences, which is infeasible
Binary classification needs many negatives, and the library has too few dissimilar images to train on
questions.explanation_en: The book says the fatal flaw isn't accuracy but the compute shape: every query must be paired with every library image. Reframed as representation learning, the library is encoded once offline and each query costs one inference plus a vector lookup. Blaming accuracy and reaching for a bigger model misses the problem reframing the chapter is really about.

questions.question: 如果对比学习的正样本只靠数据增强来造（把查询图旋转、裁剪、调色当正样本），训出来的以图搜图系统会有什么问题？
options: 数据增强产生的样本量太少，模型无法收敛，必须配合人工标注才能训练
数据增强会引入大量噪声和误点，导致模型把不相干的图片拉得很近
学到的是同一张图的形变而非同一类东西，只会返回近似重复图
数据增强会造成曝光偏差，没被展示过的图永远拿不到正标签
questions.explanation: 数据增强免费且无限，但正样本始终是同一张图的形变，模型学到的「相似」就只是近似重复。噪声和曝光偏差是用户交互这一来源的代价，不是数据增强的，这两项把不同来源的风险混在了一起。
questions.question_en: If contrastive-learning positives come only from data augmentation (rotating, cropping and recoloring the query image), what goes wrong with the resulting image search system?
options_en: Augmentation yields too few samples for the model to converge, so it must be combined with human labels to train at all
Augmentation injects lots of noise and misclicks, so the model pulls unrelated images close together
It learns distortions of the same image rather than the same kind of object, so it only returns near-duplicates
Augmentation causes exposure bias: images never shown to users can never earn positive labels
questions.explanation_en: Augmentation is free and unlimited, but every positive is a distortion of the same picture, so the learned notion of similarity collapses to near-duplicates. Noise and exposure bias are the costs of using user interactions as positives, not augmentation—those options mix up the risks of different sources.

questions.question: 以图搜图的离线评估，书里在 MRR、recall@k、precision@k、nDCG 和 mAP 中最后选了 mAP。下面哪条理由最准确？
options: mAP 只看第一个命中项的排名，最贴合用户只点第一张图的行为
相关性二元时，mAP 既看命中多少也看命中项排得是否靠前
mAP 不需要任何人工标注，可以完全从用户点击日志中计算
mAP 能同时衡量召回率、延迟和内存，是 ANN 唯一需要报告的指标
questions.explanation: 书里逐个否掉其他指标：MRR 只用第一个命中、浪费后面的信息；recall@k 需要知道全库相关项总数，视觉相似里不可知；precision@k 不管顺序；nDCG 要分级真值，成本高。「只看第一个命中项」说的其实是 MRR，正是被否掉的那个。
questions.question_en: For offline evaluation of image search, the book weighs MRR, recall@k, precision@k, nDCG and mAP, and picks mAP. Which reason is most accurate?
options_en: mAP looks only at the rank of the first hit, matching users who click only the first image
With binary relevance, mAP accounts both for how many hits there are and how high they rank
mAP needs no human labels at all and can be computed entirely from click logs
mAP captures recall, latency and memory at once, so it's the only metric ANN needs to report
questions.explanation_en: The book rules the others out one by one: MRR uses only the first hit and wastes the rest; recall@k requires knowing the total number of relevant items, which is unknowable for visual similarity; precision@k ignores order; nDCG needs graded ground truth. "Only the first hit" describes MRR—the one that was rejected.
